quarterly_data.signal: CFO Burt Podbere: Q2 FY2027 total revenue exceeded the guidance range and grew 26% over Q2 of last year to $1.47 billion, year-over-year growth accelerating sequentially for the fifth consecutive quarter; subscription revenue grew 27% to $1.40 billion and professional services revenue was an all-time record $71 million, 'as AI creates incremental demand for our AI readiness and incident response services'; revenue mix approximately 65% U.S. and 35% international, with international growth accelerating for the fifth consecutive quarter.
quarterly_data.figure: $1.47 billion total revenue, up 26% year-over-year; subscription revenue $1.40 billion, up 27%; professional services revenue $71 million

quarterly_data.signal: CEO George Kurtz and CFO Burt Podbere: all-time record net new ARR of $333 million, accelerating to 51% year-over-year growth and beating the high end of guidance by more than $45 million; ending ARR reached $5.84 billion, up more than 25% year-over-year, growth accelerating for the fourth consecutive quarter; record net new ARR from new logos, with net and gross dollar-based retention both improving sequentially; CFO: exited the quarter with a record Q3 pipeline.
quarterly_data.figure: net new ARR $333 million, up 51% year-over-year; ending ARR $5.84 billion, up more than 25%

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Burt Podbere, guidance (raised): Q3 FY2027 ARR $6.184 billion to $6.188 billion (up 26%), net new ARR $343 million to $347 million (up 29% to 31%), total revenue $1.523 billion to $1.529 billion (up 23% to 24%), non-GAAP operating income $373 million to $376 million, non-GAAP EPS approximately $0.31. Full FY2027: ARR $6.603 billion to $6.612 billion (up 26%), net new ARR $1.350 billion to $1.359 billion (up 34%; midpoint $1.355 billion, about $116 million above the initial FY2027 outlook, growth raised 1,150 basis points from 22.5% initially and from 27.7% last quarter), total revenue $5.991 billion to $6.011 billion (up 25%), non-GAAP operating income $1.497 billion to $1.508 billion, non-GAAP EPS $1.25 to $1.26; free cash flow margin expected at 27.5% in Q3 and at least 30% for the full year.
quarterly_data.figure: Q3 revenue $1.523 billion to $1.529 billion; FY revenue $5.991 billion to $6.011 billion; FY net new ARR $1.350 billion to $1.359 billion, up 34%

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Burt Podbere: Q2 non-GAAP gross margin 79%, up approximately 110 basis points; non-GAAP subscription gross margin 81%, up approximately 90 basis points on continued cloud optimization, toward the FY 2029 target model of 82%-85%; record non-GAAP operating income of $372 million, a 25% operating margin, up 350 basis points; GAAP net income attributable to CrowdStrike of $5 million (third consecutive quarter of positive GAAP earnings); non-GAAP net income a record $323 million, or $0.31 per diluted share (adjusted for the four-for-one stock split); operating cash flow a Q2 record $530 million and free cash flow a Q2 record $377 million, or 26% of revenue (above the 24.5% expectation); cash and cash equivalents $5.01 billion.
quarterly_data.figure: 79% non-GAAP gross margin; $372 million non-GAAP operating income (25% margin); $377 million free cash flow (26% of revenue)

quarterly_data.signal: CEO George Kurtz and CFO Burt Podbere: an all-time record Falcon Flex quarter - ending ARR from accounts on the Falcon Flex subscription model surpassed $2.29 billion, accelerating to 101% year-over-year growth; more than 935 Flex accounts added (more than the last three quarters combined); the top 10 deals by deal value were all Flexes; customers converting from standard subscriptions to Flex show a greater than 40% average ending ARR uplift, and a first re-Flex added a further 25% average ending ARR expansion; Flex new-logo ARR contributed a record 34% of Q2 net new ARR; more than 630 accounts have re-Flexed at least once, up 6x year-over-year; customers that re-Flexed at least twice average ending ARR 53% above their initial Flex.
quarterly_data.figure: Falcon Flex ending ARR above $2.29 billion, up 101%; 935+ Flex accounts added; 630+ re-Flexed accounts, up 6x

quarterly_data.signal: CEO George Kurtz and CFO Burt Podbere, product lines: next-gen SIEM ending ARR surpassed $695 million (CFO: up 60% year-over-year); identity ending ARR grew 34% to more than $585 million, with Falcon Shield ending ARR up more than 185% and privileged account security ending ARR up more than 35x; cloud ending ARR exceeded $905 million, up more than 29%; cloud, next-gen SIEM and next-gen identity combined ending ARR $2.1 billion, up 39%; AI Detection and Response (AI DR) ending ARR nearly tripled versus Q1; the endpoint business accelerated for the fourth consecutive quarter and exposure management accelerated sequentially; 51%, 35% and 26% of subscription customers use six, seven and eight or more modules.
quarterly_data.figure: next-gen SIEM ARR above $695 million; identity ARR above $585 million, up 34%; cloud ARR above $905 million, up 29%

quarterly_data.signal: CEO George Kurtz: AI is driving more cyber attacks and more cyber spending ('the Mythos moment turned into acceleration'); in his opinion the durability of demand 'is absolutely there'; he thinks the AI DR business can be bigger than the EDR business given the estimated number of agents per person (about 90); in sampling its customer base CrowdStrike has seen more than 400% growth in Claude usage and more than 100% growth in custom agent usage on endpoints in recent months; about half the endpoint market is still on legacy AV. AI DR is a separate, incremental, separately priced module on the same agent and already includes token-based pricing (a set number of tokens, with extra token packs) consumable through Falcon Flex.
quarterly_data.figure: 400%+ growth in Claude usage and 100%+ growth in custom agent usage on sampled customer endpoints

quarterly_data.signal: CEO George Kurtz: a frontier lab significantly grew with CrowdStrike in an eight-figure ARR Falcon Flex deal, growing Falcon Cloud Security across its rapidly expanding data center infrastructure; a mega technology conglomerate chose Falcon Cloud Security for runtime security of its AI cloud and labs in an eight-figure ARR win; frontier labs, AI-native and digital-native companies are turning to CrowdStrike, which he ties to its integration with NVIDIA's platforms ('a complete ecosystem from the chips all the way up to the applications and AI inference').

CEO George Kurtz, other Q2 wins (unnamed customers): a European automotive manufacturer replaced a next-gen EDR, a legacy SIEM and a legacy vulnerability management product in an eight-figure net new Falcon Flex; a large financial services firm replaced a next-gen EDR across more than 100 entities with two GSI partners in an eight-figure Flex; one of the world's largest banks adopted AI DR in an eight-figure Flex; a major American power provider replaced a legacy SIEM with next-gen SIEM in an eight-figure Flex; a global religious organization replaced a legacy vulnerability management product with exposure management and AI DR in a seven-figure Flex.

CEO George Kurtz, channels: more than $600 million of deal value transacted through cloud marketplaces in Q2 (AWS, Google and Microsoft), up more than 30% year-over-year, with a record Q2 at each hyperscaler marketplace; early Microsoft Marketplace wins include a seven-figure Falcon Flex with a new-logo Australian healthcare provider and a seven-figure Falcon Flex with an American manufacturing firm; Project QuiltWorks unites more than 25 partners (GSIs, hyperscalers, resellers, ISVs, distributors, MSPs) collaborating on nearly $400 million of total contract value pipeline; the GSI business grew nearly 50% year-over-year.
quarterly_data.figure: $600 million+ marketplace deal value, up 30%+; nearly $400 million QuiltWorks TCV pipeline; GSI business up nearly 50%

quarterly_data.signal: CEO George Kurtz: MSSP partner Kroll, which three quarters ago began migrating all its customers off a competing next-gen endpoint technology (a majority already migrated to Falcon across 450,000 endpoints, ahead of plan), took a multi-year Falcon Flex subscription, growing its spend with CrowdStrike by more than three times.
quarterly_data.figure: 450,000 endpoints migrated; spend up more than three times
